The current MCP service caches clients per project directory and closes their transports when that directory instance is disposed. +1 for this. A concrete use case that would benefit from agent hot-reload:

I maintain a small set of global subagents (security-review, code-review,
reviewer, implementer, etc.) where I want to swap the `model:` field per
role across a "high / medium / low" quality-vs-cost profile, switched with a
single command (a script that rewrites the `model:` line in each agent's
frontmatter). Today this requires a full OpenCode restart to take effect,
since `Agent.state` / `Config.state` are built once per instance and cached
indefinitely (confirmed by reading `packages/opencode/src/agent/agent.ts`
and `packages/opencode/src/config/config.ts` -- global config uses
`Effect.cachedInvalidateWithTTL(..., Duration.infinity)` with no file watch
invalidation).

If agent hot-reload lands, this workflow becomes truly live: switch the
active model profile mid-session without losing context, which matters a
lot for a "which model does which role" setup like this. Just flagging this
as an additional motivating use case beyond skills/commands.

1. This is a V1→V2 regression, not just a missing feature. I moved from the v1.18.31 TUI to the V2 desktop app. On v1.18.31, skills had a working invocation surface: the /skills dialog for discovery and invocation (#7846), and fully-typed /<skill-name> submission was honored even though skills were deliberately hidden from the root / autocomplete (#11547; also #43537: "typing / offered no completion even though submitting it works"). On V2 desktop (v2.0.16), skills are absent from the command registry entirely — GET /api/command returns only init and review — and I cannot find any replacement surface for discovering or invoking them. My skill workflow went from "invokable two ways" to "not invokable at all" in one migration step. I'd ask for this to be weighted as a migration regression rather than a new feature request.

2. The V2 docs already promise this behavior. The [skills docs](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/skills) state that slash defaults to shown in interactive command catalogs and slash: false hides it. The docs describe the destination state, the implementation doesn't reach it, and V1's own invocation surface got lost on the way — contract and reality currently disagree.

3. The workaround has real cost. I maintain 10 mirror files under .opencode/commands/ just to make human-invocable skills reachable via /. Every affected user builds similar scaffolding, and these will collide with native skill registration once this lands.

4. A concrete answer to the three open design questions (moved over from #40720):

Curation vs discoverability: default to showing skills in the root / list, with slash: false as the per-skill opt-out — this simply implements what the docs already specify. A global toggle can come later if noise becomes a problem.
Ordering: after built-ins and custom commands, grouped under a "Skills" section; fuzzy matching matters more than exact order.
Labeling: a :skill suffix, consistent with the existing :mcp convention.
V2 preview is exactly the right time for this behavior change, before the surface stabilizes.
5. Related compatibility gap: Claude Code's disable-model-invocation: true (human-only invocation) is currently ignored entirely — those skills are still advertised to the model and not slash-invocable, so they have no correct channel at all (#34498).

### Repro: plugin `setup` cleanup is never called when `location.reload` happens while the location is **active** (`refCount > 0`) — the old activation leaks

This looks like a **separate leak path** from the one #38825 addressed (promise-plugin `for await` not calling `return()`). On `v2` (v2.0.15) `ctx.event.subscribe` still exists, so that path was not the cause here. The maintainer note on #38825 says "no reachable repro of subscriber accumulation across location invalidate/expiry" — this is one.

#### Root cause

`LocationServiceMap.reload()` (`packages/core/src/location-service-map.ts`) calls `locations.invalidate(ref)` for every location. The custom `invalidate` in `location-services.ts` runs `inner.invalidate(key).pipe(Effect.andThen(build?.close))`, where `inner` is a `LayerMap` with `idleTimeToLive: Duration.infinity`. Effect's `RcMap.invalidate`:

```js
const entry = o.value
MutableHashMap.remove(self.state.map, key)
if (entry.refCount > 0) return          // only detaches the key, does NOT close the scope
yield* core.scopeClose(entry.scope, core.exitVoid)
```

So when a location still has an outstanding borrower (e.g. a session turn is running), the old `Instance` layer scope is **not** closed. `build.close` (`LocationLifecycle.shutdown`) detaches routing and interrupts, but the Layer scope — and therefore the plugin activation's `Effect.acquireRelease(setup, cleanup)` — is only released when refCount reaches 0. If `reload` replaces the entry, the old scope is orphaned and `cleanup` is never invoked.

#### Minimal repro (trivial promise plugin)

A plugin whose `setup` only logs and returns a cleanup that aborts its event subscription:

```ts
export default {
  id: "leak-probe",
  async setup(ctx) {
    const tag = Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 8)
    appendFileSync(LOG, `setup ${tag} loc=${ctx.location.directory}\n`)
    const abort = new AbortController()
    void (async () => {
      for await (const ev of ctx.event.subscribe({ signal: abort.signal })) { /* log */ }
    })()
    return () => { appendFileSync(LOG, `cleanup ${tag}\n`); abort.abort() }
  },
}
```

1. Send a prompt that runs ~10s in location D (keeps D borrowed).
2. While it is running, run `opencode reload`.
3. Observe the log:

```
cleanup 99iyvj loc=C:\Users\...          ← idle location: closed
cleanup x0yvc0 loc=E:\...                ← idle location: closed
setup   l0tpb9 loc=D:\...                ← D: new activation
                                         ← NO `cleanup e40c0o loc=D` (the old D activation)!
```

The old D activation (`e40c0o`) is still alive and keeps receiving `session.execution.*` from the global event stream after the reload. Idle locations are cleaned up correctly; **only the active one leaks**.

I confirmed the inverse as well: when the cleanup *is* called, `abort.abort()` stops the loop (0 further events); when a probe omits `abort()`, the old loop keeps receiving events. So the plugin-side teardown is fine — the host simply never calls it in this case.

#### Impact

- A leaked activation subscribes to the global `/api/event` stream and passes the same ownership filter, so one `session.execution.succeeded` gets delivered N times → N× auto-continuation. Measured ratio (`auto-continue receipts / succeeded`) went from `1` to `3–4` after a few reloads while a turn was in flight.
- The leaked closure retains `ctx` / location services, so memory only grows — same class of accumulation as this issue.

#### Environment

opencode `v2.0.15` (v2 branch), Windows, reproduced over the HTTP API with `opencode serve`.

The ask: `LocationServiceMap.reload()` should force-close (or wait for) the previous location scope even when it still has borrowers, instead of orphaning it. Happy to share the full probe script and logs.

### Confirming on `v2.0.15` (Windows): hot-reloading a local plugin during a turn reproduces both symptoms

Repro: a local plugin configured via `plugins` (a directory). Edit any file under its `src/**` while a session turn is running (this triggers the plugin hot-reload). Observed:

**1. The turn dies and never reaches the provider again**

```
level=ERROR message="Failed to drain Session"
cause="SessionRunnerModel.ModelUnavailableError: Model unavailable: r4-coder/deepseek-v4.1-flash
    at SessionRunnerModel.resolve
    at SessionContext.load
    at SessionRunner.advanceToStep
    at SessionRunner.drain"
```

The model is defined in `opencode.json` (a custom provider), i.e. a **config-defined model** — same shape as #47114.

**2. The session then carries the "all skills removed" instruction**

```
The following skill IDs are no longer available and must not be used:
api-and-interface-design, bootstrapblazor, brainstorming, code-simplification, ...
```

followed later by a system update re-adding them.

This is consistent with the description: a step/retry re-enters `prepareContext` → `context.select` / `resolveModel` while the catalog is half-rebuilt, after the runner already waited for activation once per drain.

**Notes**

- It is **intermittent** and usually self-heals on the next location boot, but while it lasts the turn ends `failed` and any auto-continuation loop (e.g. a goal plugin driving multi-turn work) stops until the model resolves again.
- Reproduced over the HTTP API with `opencode serve`; no provider stub needed — the failure happens before any provider request.

Additional data point: **Windows 11 + Desktop 1.18.32** — here the paste path produces a **hard renderer OOM crash**, not only a hang.

### Environment
- OpenCode Desktop **1.18.32**, Windows 11 x64
- Renderer reaches the V8 heap ceiling and is killed.

### Evidence — `%APPDATA%\ai.opencode.desktop\logs\<run>\window.log`
```
[2026-09-25 05:16:55] (window) renderer unresponsive
[2026-09-25 05:17:16] (window) app render process gone {
  url: 'oc://renderer/index.html',
  details: { reason: 'oom', exitCode: -536870904 }
}
```
Captured unresponsive samples converge on the same editor/paste path reported here:
```
HTMLDivElement.onPaste → PromptInputV2._el$6.$$input → parsePromptInputV2Editor → visit/Array.from
HTMLDivElement.onPaste → ... → setPrompt → setItem → encode → JSON.stringify
```

### Independent of session-history size (relevant to the first comment above)
The user's `opencode.db` was **9.7 GB** (dominated by a bloated `event` table). After archiving/trimming it to **1.85 GB** (`PRAGMA integrity_check = ok`), the renderer **still** OOM'd on the next large paste. So at least in this case the trigger is the **paste payload / editor serialization**, not the session history — which supports treating the paste-size path as a distinct root cause.

### Aggravating factor
Low free RAM (**1.2 GB of 15.8 GB**, due to several local MCP servers) plus a `drafts.sqlite` holding multi-MB attachment blobs. A large paste then tips the renderer over the V8 heap limit.

### Suggested mitigations
- Cap / warn on very large pastes (safe paste threshold).
- Parse and store large pasted blocks off the renderer main thread and/or in a compact representation.
- Chunk / yield during input processing; avoid repeated whole-editor traversal.
- Avoid whole-editor `JSON.stringify` on every input; avoid unnecessary reactive/layout work.

Related: #46392 (large HTML paste → renderer OOM-killed). I can provide a sanitized `window.log` if useful.

Confirming the shell-choice diagnosis with diagnostics from this machine, plus one correction to the #50950 caveat.

**`bash` resolves to WSL here, not Git Bash**

```
where.exe bash  -> C:\Users\gomez\AppData\Local\Microsoft\WindowsApps\bash.exe
bash --version  -> GNU bash, version 5.3.9(1)-release (x86_64-pc-linux-gnu)
```

Git Bash is installed at `C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe`, but only `Git\cmd` is on PATH, so `bash` falls through to the WSL alias. `OPENCODE_GIT_BASH_PATH` is unset here. (FYI `C:\Windows\System32\bash.exe` does not exist on this machine — the stub is the WindowsApps alias.)

**#50950 does not need a second cause**

I reproduced that exact text with the script present:

```
bash "C:\Users\gomez\.cache\opencode\zz-test-bash\install" --version
/bin/bash: C:\Users\gomez\.cache\opencode\zz-test-bash\install: No such file or directory
```

The file was verified present before and after. WSL bash words a Windows path like that with the backslashes intact, so nothing has to remove it between download and exec. Nothing on this machine touches `.cache\opencode\update-*`.

**Small nuance for the fix**

A Git-Bash-style conversion (`/c/Users/...`) also fails in WSL bash with the same message — only `/mnt/c/...` would actually run it. So the MINGW/MSYS/CYGWIN guard is the right fix, but a naive conversion fails safe rather than installing a Linux binary.

I'd like to work on this one (I'm on Windows, so I can test the real locking case).

From reading `v2`: `Worktree.remove` in `packages/core/src/worktree.ts` calls the git strategy without releasing cached Locations for that directory, so a stdio MCP server started with `cwd` = the worktree still holds the directory. Refresh only drops rows whose directory is missing, so the empty leftover keeps its row and every retry hits `DirectoryUnavailableError`.

Plan:
1. Before strategy removal, evict cached local Locations at or under the worktree path (same mechanism as `debug.location.evict`) so their MCP/PTY finalizers run first.
2. Let retry/refresh clean up a saved git worktree row whose directory is empty and no longer registered with git. Non-empty directories are left alone.
3. Regression tests that don't depend on Windows file locking: ordering (Location finalizers finish before git removal) and the empty-leftover state.

One question: if a session is still running in that worktree, should remove fail with a clear error, or interrupt and wait like the inactivity sweep in `location-activity.ts`? I'd default to failing with an error unless you prefer otherwise.

Root-caused this one (and #50336 — same bug) on v2.0.16.

`Prompt.Base64` in `packages/schema/src/prompt.ts` validates with

```ts
/^(?:[A-Za-z0-9+/]{4})*(?:[A-Za-z0-9+/]{2}==|[A-Za-z0-9+/]{3}=)?$/
```

Regex engines recurse per iteration of the `(?:…{4})*` group, so past a few MB the check stops working. Under Bun 1.4.2/JSC (the runtime embedded in the shipped binary) it silently returns `false` for canonical base64 — that's the `InvalidValue` schema issue in the 500 logs from `POST /api/session/<id>/prompt`. Under V8 the same input throws RangeError instead. `materializeAttachment` base64-encodes attachments up to the 20 MB limit and runs this check on the result, so any `@`-attached file over roughly 5 MB (any type — PDF, xlsx, …) fails the prompt with a 500 before the provider is called. Small attachments pass, which is why images seem fine.

Minimal repro:

```js
const re = /^(?:[A-Za-z0-9+/]{4})*(?:[A-Za-z0-9+/]{2}==|[A-Za-z0-9+/]{3}=)?$/
const s = require("crypto").randomBytes(20 * 1024 * 1024).toString("base64")
re.test(s) // Bun/JSC: false (canonical base64!) · Node/V8: RangeError
```

The grouped-quantifier shape can't be fixed with a better regex. Canonical base64 is decidable with a length preflight plus a structurally linear pattern (a single char-class star compiles iteratively, no recursion):

```ts
const n = s.length
if (n % 4 !== 0) return false
if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9+/]*={0,2}$/.test(s)) return false
const pads = s.endsWith("==") ? 2 : s.endsWith("=") ? 1 : 0
return (n - pads) % 4 !== 1
```

I fuzzed 20k mutated canonical strings against both — zero mismatches (`AB==`/`ABC=` accept, `AB=`/`ABCD==`/`A===` reject, `""` accepted, base64url `-_` rejected, same as the current pattern). The 27.9M-char encoding of a 20 MB file passes in 6 ms; the current pattern returns `false` on it in 156 ms under Bun 1.4.2.

Happy to send a PR if useful.

Same root cause as #45558: the `Prompt.Base64` pattern check in `packages/schema/src/prompt.ts` uses a `(?:X{4})*` regex that fails on multi-MB strings (silently returns `false` under Bun/JSC, the runtime the shipped binary embeds; throws RangeError under V8). `materializeAttachment` runs it on the base64 of any `@`-mentioned file up to 20 MB, which is why a 12 MB xlsx crashes the prompt while small files work. Analysis, repro, and a parity-safe replacement in #45558 — a PR referencing both issues is on the way.

Local workaround verified: all 113 old rows in `session_v2` had `project_id='global'` (worktree `/`) with directories under `/home/foxkovsky`, while V2 created project `9c1236c28ccbabd065b67815c9b78f013475e8a4` (canonical `/home/foxkovsky`). After backing up `opencode.db` (sqlite backup API, no service stop) I ran: `UPDATE session_v2 SET project_id='<new>' WHERE project_id='global' AND (directory='/home/foxkovsky' OR directory LIKE '/home/foxkovsky/%')` (same for legacy `session` table). Filtered `GET /api/session?directory=/home/foxkovsky` now returns the old sessions (50 on first page, all with the new projectID) instead of just 1. Suggests migration should reassign sessions whose directory falls under a newly detected project worktree, or the session list should span ancestor/descendant projects.

Update: project_id alone was not enough. Old rows also had a stale `path` (subpath relative to old worktree `/`, e.g. `path='home/foxkovsky'`), while V2 sessions at the project root use `path=''`. The TUI session picker filters on that too, so I recomputed `path` relative to the new worktree `/home/foxkovsky` (root sessions -> `''`, subdir sessions -> relative remainder, e.g. `'Документы/...'`). 113 rows fixed in both `session_v2` and legacy `session`. Now `GET /api/session/<old-id>` returns `location:{directory:/home/foxkovsky}` with no `subpath`, identical in shape to a native V2 session, and the filtered list returns them. Full migration needs both: `project_id` AND `path` recomputed against the new project worktree.

## Update (2026-09-25): default-model resolution, sanitizer infeasibility, scope

Continued probing on an isolated replica of the same 2.0.16 build (fresh `opencode serve` on a scratch port, live env replicated, same plugin set, XDG tree isolated) added four facts.

### 1. Default model resolution for API-created sessions → built-in `opencode/space-bunny-free`

- `POST /session` without a model pin resolves to `opencode/space-bunny-free` (built-in zen free model) **at execution time** — the session object reports `model: null` at creation; resolution happens later.
- This occurs even when the config carries `model` / `default_agent` defaults — those are ignored for API-created sessions.
- The resolution is not gated by anything we could find:
  - `disabled_providers: ["opencode", "anthropic"]` in config: no effect.
  - Stripping `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` / `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` env: no effect (with `ANTHROPIC_MODEL=deepseek-v4-flash-free` set, resolution still lands on `space-bunny-free`).
  - No stored zen credentials exist in the data dir (no `auth.json` / storage entries).
- Explicit pin at creation works: `{"model":{"providerID":"llama-server","id":"coder"}}` (both fields required; `id` alone → 400).
- **Why it matters for this issue:** the Class B failure reproduces deterministically on default-resolved sessions — every unpinned API-created session on 2.0.16 hits `Schema validation failed` regardless of provider/model config. Any client that creates unpinned sessions (not just OpenChamber's subagents) is affected.

### 2. A plugin-side sanitizer is infeasible (index-shift test)

- A marker plugin pushing a valid `{type:"text"}` part into `event.system` inside the `context` hook **does propagate into the final request**: the failing index shifted `system[4]` → `system[5]` (no-marker runs: 57 consecutive retries failing at `[4]`; marker runs: 92 consecutive retries failing at `[5]`, marker's post-push array length = 5).
- Therefore the invalid part is appended by **core after all `context` hooks run** — it is always the *last* system part of the assembled array.
- No plugin-visible hook exposes the final system array: observed payloads are `context` [4 valid parts], `prompt` [no system field], `title` [1 part]; `execution.failed` carries no system payload. Hooks also receive separate event copies (one observer saw 4 parts while a concurrent hook's copy already had 5).
- Conclusion: the invalid part cannot be intercepted or fixed from a plugin; the fix must be in core request assembly. (For reference, the invalid part's content is only visible in the server log's `cause` payload — `{"~effect/SchemaIssue/Issue"…}` with `Pointer(path=[4|5])` → `InvalidType` — not in any hook payload.)

### 3. Scope refinement

| session type | model | system parts at `context` hook | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| main session (UI, pinned) | llama-server/coder | 4 valid | works |
| subagent child | llama-server/small-model or coder | 4 valid | fails `system[4]` |
| API-created, unpinned | resolves to `opencode/space-bunny-free` | 4 valid | fails `system[4]` |
| compaction child | llama-server/small-notools | (same path) | fails (per original report) |
| title child | resolves to `opencode/space-bunny-free` | 1 | **does not fail** |

So the invalid part is appended on the child/auxiliary session assembly path (subagent + unpinned API sessions + compaction), while the title child (single system part) and main session pass. Not model-dependent, not provider-dependent, not length-dependent.

### 4. Secondary local-model finding (separate from this bug)

Pinned `llama-server/*` sessions on a llama-swap `-np 1` (single-slot) backend can fail **immediately with `provider.no-route: Model unavailable` when the alias's model is not the currently loaded one — before request assembly at all (no `context` hook event fires)**. With a shared single-slot backend this makes even the working main-session model intermittently unroutable for concurrent

## Correction: the root cause is a missing i18n key, not malformed session data

The original version of this issue blamed a `tool` part whose name was `undefined`. That was wrong, and I have updated the issue body with the verified cause.

最初版本把根因归结为「某个 tool part 的 name 为 `undefined`」，这是错误的。正文已更正为经验证的真正原因。

I scanned every `tool`/`shell` part in the database: all 223 in the affected session have valid string names, and a database-wide scan found zero with a missing name. The `undefined` is produced at render time instead:

我扫描了数据库中所有 `tool`/`shell` part——该会话的 223 个全部是合法字符串 name，全库扫描也没有任何一个缺 name。这个 `undefined` 是渲染时产生的：

- `sC()`'s `todowrite` branch calls `r.t('ui.tool.todos')`, and **`ui.tool.todos` does not exist in the locale catalogue**
- `ZT()` (the implementation behind `t()`) returns `undefined` for an unknown key — there is no fallback
- `fC()` passes that `undefined` into `t.list()`, and only the non-`en` branch (`Intl.ListFormat#format`) rejects it

- `sC()` 的 `todowrite` 分支调用 `r.t('ui.tool.todos')`，而 **`ui.tool.todos` 在语言包中不存在**
- `t()` 底层的 `ZT()` 对未知 key 返回 `undefined`，没有任何兜底
- `fC()` 把这个 `undefined` 传给 `t.list()`，只有非 `en` 分支（`Intl.ListFormat#format`）会拒绝它

So the trigger is "a session containing a `todowrite` call" plus "a non-English locale", not one particular session. In my database 35 of 139 sessions contain a `todowrite` call and would be affected.

因此触发条件是「会话包含 `todowrite` 调用」+「非英语 locale」，而非某个特定会话。我的数据库中 139 个会话有 35 个包含 `todowrite` 调用，都会受影响。

Thanks for confirming the diagnosis and for offering to work on a fix.

My preference is the robust version:

1. Add the missing `ui.tool.todos` English fallback.
2. Harden `createUiI18n().list()` so `undefined` or other non-string entries cannot crash the session timeline, including malformed tool parts like the one described in #51286.
3. Add regression tests for both a missing translation and a malformed or missing tool name.

For translations, I prefer adding the English fallback and adding other translations only when they can be verified, rather than machine-translating every locale file.

Two scope corrections from further testing (2.0.16, same build):

**1. Native auto-compaction is NOT broken — subagent child sessions are.**
`GET /api/session/:id/context` on a live 2.0.16 server shows a native compaction
item with `status: "completed"`, `reason: "auto"`, `model: llama-server/coder`,
created after the 2.0.16 server started. So the built-in compaction child
session avoids this issue just like the 1-part `title` child session. The
failing class is narrower than the original report said: **child sessions whose
request assembles the full 4-part build system** (subagent dispatch, and
unpinned client sessions that resolve to a model at execution time).
Main sessions, title, and compaction child sessions all succeed.

**2. `/api/experimental/generate` is a working bypass for plugin-side work.**
`POST /api/experimental/generate` with `{"prompt": "...", "model": {"providerID": "...", "id": "..."}}`
returns `{"data": {"text": "..."}}` (200) on 2.0.16 — direct server-side
generation with no child session, so it cannot hit the assembly path. Without a
model it 400s ("No model specified and no supported model is available"). There
is no message-level write API (`DELETE/PUT/POST /api/session/:id/message/:mid`
all 404), so plugins can only affect the *request* (context-hook in-place
mutation), which is exactly what a working request-level compression plugin
already does in production.

Related context for anyone following this: unpinned API-created sessions
resolve to `opencode/space-bunny-free` at execution time (previous comment), so
any client that doesn't pin a model per session (OpenChamber does pin) will
keep hitting this.

@vshulcz That 1,096 vs 80,547 token benchmark is a fantastic empirical result—it cleanly proves that selective passage recall beats raw transcript replay by ~73x. And your observation that zero users run manual `promote --state superseded` across 1,160 sessions matches reality: if memory maintenance requires active human curation, it doesn't happen.

Your trade-off analysis hits the exact architectural frontier:
> *"i take that trade knowingly, since a ledger has to pick the fact at write time and the transcript is gone when it picks wrong. but you are right that it costs context on every prompt."*

The way we resolve that false dilemma in **Smriti** (our dedicated bi-temporal knowledge graph engine) is by treating the architecture as a **Two-Tier Ledger & Evidence Hybrid**:

1. **Tier 1 (The Immutable Evidence Store):** The raw session transcript and tool outputs are never thrown away. They are stored in an append-only event log referenced by an immutable hash (`source_session_id`, `receipt_digest`). When a developer needs forensic debugging or an agent needs to audit *why* a decision was made, the full raw dialogue remains accessible.
2. **Tier 2 (The Bi-Temporal Fact Ledger):** Structured SVO assertions (`[Auth] -> [Uses] -> [JWT]`) live in a relational layer with explicit chronological validity (`valid_from`, `valid_to`). When a new verified decision is recorded, it closes the previous assertion (`valid_to = now()`), binding the pointer to the Tier 1 receipt digest.
3. **Non-Destructive Re-extraction:** If an automated extraction ever extracts the wrong fact, the underlying transcript is still intact. A re-indexing run or explicit correction simply invalidates the flawed triple and mints a corrected one, preserving complete provenance.

By decoupling the active prompt context (`WHERE valid_to IS NULL` costing ~80 tokens) from the historical evidence store, the model gets clean, zero-contradiction startup orientation without losing transcript forensic fidelity.

For OpenCode and `deja-vu`, a lightweight SQLite implementation of this split (a `facts` table with `valid_to` referencing passage hashes in `deja.db`) could allow callers to request `--mode active` ($O(1)$ facts) or `--mode forensic` (dated passage overlap), bridging the gap between prompt economy and audit safety.

Still hit this in **1.18.32** (newer than the 1.18.25 / 1.18.29 verified versions in this thread). Same LiteLLM OpenAI-compatible custom-provider scenario as @eddoww — `litellm.hhstaging.dev/v1` proxying `minimax/MiniMax-M3` (model advertises `supports_vision: true` in the litellm admin UI and accepts the same base64 image_url payload via direct `curl` with `200 + correct description`).

`opencode.jsonc`:
```jsonc
"minimax/MiniMax-M3": {
  "name": "MiniMax M3",
  "attachment": true,
  "modalities": { "input": ["text", "image"] }
}
```

Read tool still returns:
```
ERROR: Cannot read "screenshot.png" (this model does not support image input)
```

**Root cause in the binary** (verified by `strings` on the embedded JS bundle in `opencode 1.18.32`): the conversion cascade for user-defined custom-provider models ends up with `Z.capabilities.input` as an **array** `["text","image"]`, but the read tool's filter does `Z.capabilities.input[W]` (array index-by-string → `undefined`). The object form `{image: true, ...}` is only populated when a `models.dev` registry entry exists for the model (`J.input_modalities?.includes("image")`); for custom aliases with no registry entry the cascade falls through to `Y?.capabilities.input.image`, which is never set because the public user schema doesn't expose `capabilities`.

The exact gating line in the read-tool message filter:
```js
if (Z.capabilities.input[W]) return J;          // W = "image"
return { type: "text", text: `ERROR: Cannot read ${G ?? W} (this model does not support ${W} input). Inform the user.` };
```

**Workarounds tried, both inert in 1.18.32:**
- `attachment: true` — sets a separate `capabilities.attachment` bool used by the UI affordance; does not populate `capabilities.input.image`.
- `modalities: { input: ["text", "image"] }` — copied into `capabilities.input` as an array, but the read tool's key lookup still misses.

**Suggested fix:** in the user-config → internal-model converter, when no `models.dev` entry exists for the model, translate `modalities.input[]` into the object form so `capabilities.input.image` resolves truthy for the read-tool filter. Or expose `capabilities` (or just `capabilities.input: { image?: boolean, ... }`) as a user schema field with the same boolean keys the resolver already consumes.

Until then, this binary is unusable for vision via custom-provider aliases — even when the upstream endpoint is fully vision-capable.

Code-level follow-up from the same environment (OpenCode 2.0.16, subtracted to current `v2` HEAD `048a47e8`).

**The stall mechanism is visible in source.** On `v2` HEAD:

- `packages/core/src/session/runner/llm.ts:332` `settleStaleToolCalls` only runs on drain entry (next turn): it publishes `Tool.Failed` for parts stuck in `streaming`/`running`. There is no in-process watchdog that fires while the request itself is stalled.
- `packages/core/src/aisdk.ts:161`: `if (!chunkAbortCtl || typeof chunkTimeout !== 'number') return res` — with no user-configured `provider.<id>.options.chunkTimeout` (optional, no default; `model-resolver.ts:393` passes through possibly-undefined), the SSE response is returned unwrapped with no inter-chunk timer. A silently-dead stream then waits forever.
- None of the 46 commits between `v2.0.16` (`3a103fe0`) and current `v2` HEAD touch this path (only compaction-overflow revert/reland and batched deltas near the runner).

So the observable bug stands on current `v2`: opt-in watchdog, off by default, plus wake-only stale settlement. Workaround for anyone hitting this: set `chunkTimeout` on the provider. Happy to test a default-timer or drain-independent reaper if one is proposed.
